# Data wrangling

```{r}
combined_df <- read_csv("./Data/10_count_env_df.csv")

df <- combined_df |> 
  mutate(
    wind_speed.night = sqrt(uwind.10m.night^2 + vwind.10m.night^2),
    colony = as.factor(colony),
    year = as.factor(year),
    roost_type = as.factor(roost_type),
    local_date = as.Date(local_date)
  ) |> 
  
  # --- Collapse multiple per-night tracks into one row per colony-night ---
  # track_90q_count and track_count_se are recalculated, allowing only one per colony-night
  # adjusted_VIC is the raw per-track value
  # (potentially) multiple tracks exist per night per cplony, currently considered as one.
  group_by(colony, local_date) |> 
  arrange(from_sunset) |> 
  summarise(
    track_90q_count = quantile(adjusted_VIC, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    track_count_se  = sd(adjusted_VIC, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    n_tracks        = n(),                     # keep this — useful diagnostic, see note below
    
    # Environmental covariates should be constant within a colony-night;
    # take the first value per group, but see the warning below.
    across(
      c(ctr_lon, ctr_lat, year, yday,
        air.2m.night, air.2m.night.diff, wind_speed.night, 
        prate.night, avg_drought_index,
        rhum.2m.night, pres.sfc.night, tcdc.night, lunar.illumination,
        from_sunset, dist, roost_type),
      ~ first(.x)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 

# rebuild series_id for the ar() grouping using AR.start blocks rather than calendar year (since a colony's monitoring can have gaps that calendar year doesn't capture)
```

Addtionally (not done yet), I could consider whether n_tracks (how many radar tracks contributed to each night's 90th percentile) should enter the model. A 90th percentile computed from 3 tracks is a much noisier estimate of "true" nightly emergence intensity than one computed from 50 tracks. This is exactly what track_count_se was meant to capture, but I could also:

-   Filter out very low-n_tracks nights if they're likely unreliable (e.g., n_tracks \< 5), or

-   Weight the model by track_count_se (e.g., via weights = 1/track_count_se\^2 in bam, or as a measurement-error model in brms) rather than treating every night's response as equally precise.

```{r}
mean(dist(df_colony[, c("ctr_lon", "ctr_lat")])) / 1000
```

## The 3-Day Rolling Average

Test compensatory foraging: bats "penned up" by bad weather will emerge in much higher intensity on subsequent nights. 
series_id: a continuous, uninterrupted sequence of nights for a single colony. Every time there is a data gap of more than one day (time_diff > 1), bout_id increments, creating a brand new series_id.

```{r}
library(slider)
library(lubridate)

track_df <- df |> 
  # --- 3-day rolling average of PRIOR emergence (compensatory foraging test) ---
  group_by(colony) |> 
  arrange(local_date) |> 
  mutate(
    avg_3day_prior = slide_index_dbl(
      .x = track_90q_count,
      .i = local_date,
      .f = mean,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      .before = days(2),
      .after  = days(-1)   # excludes current night; window = t-3 to t-1
    )
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  
  # Drop rows without enough history for the lag
  filter(!is.na(avg_3day_prior), !is.nan(avg_3day_prior)) |> 
  
  # --- Recompute AR structure on the FILTERED series ---
  # This must happen after filtering, since dropped rows change where each
  # colony's usable series actually begins and where gaps now fall.
  arrange(colony, local_date) |> 
  group_by(colony) |> 
  mutate(
    time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(local_date, lag(local_date), units = "days")),
    AR.start  = ifelse(is.na(time_diff) | time_diff > 1, TRUE, FALSE),
    bout_id   = cumsum(AR.start)
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(series_id = interaction(colony, bout_id, drop = TRUE))

track_df <- track_df |>
  arrange(colony, local_date) |>
  group_by(colony) |>
  mutate(
    prate.night.diff = prate.night - lag(prate.night)   # change in precip, not raw lag
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

Replaced the year/yday-based series_id at the bottom with the AR.start/bout_id approach from before, computed fresh on the filtered data using local_date (real calendar time) rather than yday (which resets every Jan 1 and would incorrectly treat Dec 31 → Jan 1 as a huge "gap" even if monitoring was continuous, or wrongly link two unrelated Jan-1-adjacent nights across different years).

Check for correlations and concurvity

```{r}
# Quick linear correlation as a first pass (won't catch nonlinear concurvity, but fast)
cor(track_df$rhum.2m.night, track_df$prate.night, use = "complete.obs")
cor(track_df$rhum.2m.night, track_df$prate.night.diff, use = "complete.obs")
cor(track_df$prate.night, track_df$avg_3day_prior, use = "complete.obs")

quick_check <- bam(
  log(track_90q_count) ~
    s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) +
    s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination) + s(avg_drought_index) +
    s(from_sunset) + s(dist) + s(avg_3day_prior) +

    roost_type +
    s(colony, bs = "re") + s(year, bs = "re"),
  data = track_df, method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE
)

# Overview: one value per term (how well is each term predicted by ALL the others?)
conc_full <- concurvity(quick_check, full = TRUE)
round(conc_full$observed, 2)
round(conc_full$estimate, 2)

# Pairwise: identifies WHICH terms are the partners
conc_pair <- concurvity(quick_check, full = FALSE)
obs <- conc_pair$observed
obs[upper.tri(obs, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
idx <- which(obs > 0.7, arr.ind = TRUE)
data.frame(term1 = rownames(obs)[idx[, 1]],
           term2 = colnames(obs)[idx[, 2]],
           concurvity = obs[idx])

quick_check <- bam(

)

track_df$rhum_resid <- residuals(resid_model)

quick_check <- bam(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night) + 
    s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) + s(prate.night) +

)

resid_model <- bam(avg_3day_prior ~ s(prate.night), data = track_df, method = "fREML")
summary(resid_model) # Because both avg_3day_prior & prate.night are heavily skewed (one with millions of zeros, one with extreme values out to $5\times 10^6$), both basis expansions struggle to separate cleanly from the global intercept (para). ## Variables and hypothesis
```

-   avg_3day_prior (Behavioral momentum / Compensatory foraging)

-   air.2m.night (Thermal constraint)

-   air.2m.night.diff (Relative temperature change as a phenological trigger)

-   wind_speed.night (Flight aerodynamic cost)

-   prate.night (Direct flight impairment)

-   rhum.2m.night (Often tied to insect abundance)

-   pres.sfc.night (Barometric pressure changes often cue insect hatches and bat activity)

-   tcdc.night (Cloud cover)

-   lunar.illumination (Predator avoidance / visual acuity)

-   avg_drought_index (Long-term habitat/prey productivity constraint)

# Bayesian mixed-effects analysis

The comparison set

1.  Baseline: no AR, no factor-smooth — tests whether the temporal/colony-phenology structure is worth the computational cost at all
2.  AR(1), no factor-smooth — isolates the effect of the AR term alone
3.  factor-smooth, no AR — isolates the effect of colony-specific phenology alone
4.  Your full model (both AR + factor-smooth) — coded below
5.  colony size, + targeted interactions — the "performance-chasing" version, built once you know which interactions RF flags (from your earlier plan)
6.  Simplified colony-slope alternative to the factor-smooth — worth testing since s(yday,colony,bs="fs") is by far your most expensive term (371 basis functions in the frequentist fit); a random-slope version is much cheaper and might capture almost as much

Distributional family alternatives

Worth testing at least one alongside the family sweep, since log(y) \~ gaussian is a pragmatic default, not a verified-best choice:

-   gaussian() on log(y) — what you have now

-   Gamma(link = "log") on raw track_90q_count — often more appropriate for strictly-positive, right-skewed count-like data than log-transform + gaussian, and avoids the (common but easy-to-miss) issue that log(y) \~ N implicitly assumes multiplicative log-normal errors, which may not match your residual distribution

-   brms::negbinomial() on raw counts — closest to what you already did for the colony-trend models, appropriate if track_90q_count is still meaningfully integer-like (a 90th-percentile of detection counts might be) rather than continuous

Run order (given compute cost)

1.  Fit models 1, 2, 3 (base, +AR, +factor-smooth) first — cheapest, and this tells you whether AR and/or factor-smooth are worth their cost at all, using loo_compare() as an approximate first pass.

2.  Fit model 6 (random slope) as a cheaper alternative to the factor-smooth — compare against model 3/4 to see how much you lose by simplifying.

3.  Once you know which structural pieces matter, fit the family sweep (Gamma, negbinomial) only on your best structural formula, comparing via CV RMSE on the raw scale.

4.  Only then invest in model 5 (interactions + colony size) informed by the RF exploration step, since it's the most expensive and most complexity-adding version — you want to know the cheaper pieces are justified before stacking more on top.

This ordering also gives you a natural table for your methods/results section: a nested model comparison showing which components (AR, colony-phenology, interactions, distributional family) each contributed to fit, rather than presenting only the final "kitchen sink" model with no justification for its complexity.

```{r}
library(brms)

track_df = read_csv("./Data/track_df.csv")

# base model
base = bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + (1 | colony) + (1 | year) 
)

# AR(1) only model
ar_only = bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + (1 | colony) + (1 | year) + 
    ar(time = local_date, gr = series_id, p = 1) 
)

# random slope + AR(1) model
# captures colony-specific linear pattern changes rather than fully flexible nonlinear ones
ranslope_ar = bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night, k = 10) + s(pres.sfc.night, by = roost_type, k = 10, m = 1) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + 
    (1 + yday | colony) + (1 | year) + 
    ar(time = local_date, gr = series_id, p = 1) 
)

# factor-smooth only model
fs_only = bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + 
    s(yday, colony, bs = "fs", xt = list(bs = "cc"), k = 8) + 
    (1 | colony) + (1 | year) 
)

# full model
fs_ar <- bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + 
    s(yday, colony, bs = "fs", xt = list(bs = "cc"), k = 8) + 
    (1 | colony) + (1 | year) + 
    ar(time = local_date, gr = series_id, p = 1)
)

# full model + interaction
fs_ar_interact = bf(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) + s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum_resid) + s(pres.sfc.night, k = 10) + s(pres.sfc.night, by = roost_type, k = 10, m = 1) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) + s(avg_drought_index) + roost_type + s(dist) + s(from_sunset) + s(avg_3day_prior) + s(yday, bs = "cc") + s(yday, colony, bs = "fs", xt = list(bs = "cc"), k = 8) + (1 | colony) + (1 | year) + ar(time = local_date, gr = series_id, p = 1) 
)

# Check what priors brms expects for this formula before fitting
get_prior(fs_ar, data = track_df, family = gaussian())

priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b"),                 # fixed effects (roost_type)
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds"),        # smooth term wiggliness (all s() terms)
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sd"),         # colony/year random intercept SDs
  prior(normal(0, 0.3), class = "ar"),               # AR(1) coefficient — you already know it's small (~0.06)
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sigma")       # residual SD
)

```

```{r}
library(cmdstanr)
# Ensure output directory exists
dir.create("./Models/csvs", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

fit <- brm(
  fs_ar,
  data = track_df,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = priors,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",     # substantially faster than rstan for this size
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
  seed = 123,
  output_dir = "./Models/csvs"  # <-- Saves raw chain CSVs here permanently
)
```

Diagnostics and model checking

```{r}
# Convergence
summary(fit)              # check Rhat ~1.00, adequate Bulk_ESS/Tail_ESS
plot(fit)                 # trace plots for key parameters

# Posterior predictive check — does simulated data resemble observed?
pp_check(fit, ndraws = 100)

# Smooth term visualization with credible intervals
conditional_smooths(fit)

# AR(1) coefficient posterior — compare to BAM point estimate of 0.063
posterior_summary(fit, variable = "ar[1]")

# Model comparison (e.g., with vs without AR term) via LOO
# fit_no_ar <- update(fit, formula. = bf_model_without_ar, ...)
loo(fit, fit_no_ar)
```

## Compare models

Standard loo() is compromised here because of the ar() term — PSIS-LOO assumes exchangeable observations, but with an AR(1) structure, leaving out a single time point conditional on its neighbors isn't a well-posed leave-one-out problem in the usual sense (brms will warn about this, or pareto_k diagnostics may look unreliable specifically in the presence of autocor() terms). Options:

1.  loo() anyway, but treat results as approximate/exploratory — useful for the non-AR comparisons (models 1, 3, 6-without-ar) and as a rough signal for the AR models, but don't over-interpret small ELPD differences for anything with ar():

```{r}
library(loo)
fit_base <- readRDS("./Models/base.rds")
fit_ar   <- readRDS("./Models/ar_only.rds")
fit_fs   <- readRDS("./Models/fs_only.rds")
fit_full <- readRDS("./Models/fs_ar.rds")
fit_fs_ar_interact = readRDS("./Models/fs_ar_interact.rds")
fit_ranslope_ar = readRDS("./Models/ranslope_ar.rds")

loo_base <- loo(fit_base)
loo_ar   <- loo(fit_ar)
loo_fs   <- loo(fit_fs)
loo_full <- loo(fit_full)
loo_fs_ar_interact = loo(fit_fs_ar_interact)
loo_ranslope = loo(fit_ranslope_ar)

loo_compare(loo_base, loo_ar, loo_fs, loo_full, loo_fs_ar_interact, loo_ranslope)

saveRDS(loo_base, "./Models/loo_base.rds")
saveRDS(loo_fs, "./Models/loo_fs.rds")
saveRDS(loo_ar, "./Models/loo_ar.rds")
saveRDS(loo_full, "./Models/loo_full.rds")
saveRDS(loo_fs_ar_interact, "./Models/loo_fs_ar_interact.rds")
saveRDS(loo_ranslope, "./Models/loo_ranslope.rds")
```

## K-fold

k_psis > 0.7 means PSIS-LOO's importance sampling approximation is unreliable for that specific observation in fit_fs and fit_full — the elpd contribution from that one point could be biased, which could specifically affect exactly the comparison you care about (full vs. fs).

blocked/grouped k-fold CV — hold out entire series_id blocks (whole colony-seasons) rather than individual nights, so temporal dependency within a held-out block stays intact and prediction is genuinely out-of-sample:

```{r}
options(future.globals.maxSize = 3 * 1024^3)
kfold_cv <- kfold(fit_full, K = 5, folds = "grouped", group = "series_id")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(brms)
library(Metrics) # for rmse, mae

# 1. Create a blocked split (e.g., hold out 20% of series_ids)
set.seed(123)
all_series <- unique(track_df$series_id)
test_series <- sample(all_series, size = length(all_series) * 0.2)

train_df <- track_df |> filter(!series_id %in% test_series)
test_df  <- track_df |> filter(series_id %in% test_series)

# 2. Refit the model on the training data 
# (using update() is faster as it avoids recompiling the Stan code)
fit_train <- update(fit_full, newdata = train_df)

# 3. Predict on the hold-out test set
# allow_new_levels = TRUE is necessary if any colonies in the test set weren't in the train set
preds <- predict(fit_train, newdata = test_df, allow_new_levels = TRUE)

# predict() returns a matrix with Estimate, Est.Error, Q2.5, Q97.5
test_df$pred_log_count <- preds[, "Estimate"]

# 4. Exponentiate back to original scale for ML evaluation
test_df <- test_df |> 
  mutate(
    pred_count = exp(pred_log_count),
    obs_count = track_90q_count
  )

# 5. Calculate ML-style metrics
out_of_sample_rmse <- rmse(test_df$obs_count, test_df$pred_count)
out_of_sample_mae <- mae(test_df$obs_count, test_df$pred_count)
```

## Check for spatial autocorrelation

```{r}
library(ape)
fit = readRDS("./Models/fs_ar.rds")

colony_resid <- track_df |>
  mutate(resid = residuals(fit)[, "Estimate"]) |>
  group_by(colony) |>
  summarise(mean_resid = mean(resid, na.rm = TRUE),
            ctr_lon = first(ctr_lon), ctr_lat = first(ctr_lat))

dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(colony_resid[, c("ctr_lon","ctr_lat")]))
inv_dist <- 1 / dist_mat
diag(inv_dist) <- 0

Moran.I(colony_resid$mean_resid, inv_dist)
# no statistically significant spatial autocorrelation in your colony-level mean residuals ($p = 0.745)
```

```{r}
# )

# --- 1b. Helper to build one panel matching the reference style:
#   solid line, dashed CI, rug marks on x-axis, back-transformed to count scale ---
make_smooth_panel <- function(cs_obj, xvar, xlab, raw_data_col = NULL) {
  # Find the matching slot in cs containing the variable name
  matched_name <- grep(paste0("\\b", xvar, "\\b"), names(cs_obj), value = TRUE)
  
  if (length(matched_name) == 0) {
    stop(paste("No smooth found matching variable:", xvar))
  }
  
  cs_df <- cs_obj[[matched_name[1]]]
  cs_df <- cs_df %>%
    mutate(
      estimate_bt = exp(estimate__),
      lower_bt    = exp(lower__),
      upper_bt    = exp(upper__)
    )
 
  p <- ggplot(cs_df, aes(x = .data[[xvar]], y = estimate_bt)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_line(aes(y = lower_bt), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(aes(y = upper_bt), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Partial effect") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_blank())
 
  # add rug marks from the raw covariate distribution, as in the reference figure
  if (!is.null(raw_data_col)) {
    p <- p + geom_rug(
      data = track_df, aes(x = .data[[raw_data_col]], y = NULL),
      sides = "b", alpha = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  }
  p
}
 
# --- 1c. Build each panel; MAP actual smooth term names here.
 
panel_list <- list(
  A = make_smooth_panel(cs, "air.2m.night",       "Air temperature (K)",            "air.2m.night"),
  B = make_smooth_panel(cs, "pres.sfc.night",      "Surface pressure",               "pres.sfc.night"),
  C = make_smooth_panel(cs, "rhum_resid",          "Relative humidity (residual)",   "rhum_resid"),
  D = make_smooth_panel(cs, "tcdc.night",          "Total cloud cover (%)",          "tcdc.night"),
  E = make_smooth_panel(cs, "wind_speed.night",    "Wind speed (m/s)",               "wind_speed.night"),
  F = make_smooth_panel(cs, "prate.night",         "Precipitation rate",             "prate.night"),
  H = make_smooth_panel(cs, "air.2m.night.diff",   "Night air temp difference (K)",  "air.2m.night.diff"),
  I = make_smooth_panel(cs, "avg_drought_index",   "Palmer drought index",           "avg_drought_index"),
  J = make_smooth_panel(cs, "from_sunset",         "Time from sunset (mins)",        "from_sunset"),
  K = make_smooth_panel(cs, "lunar.illumination",  "Lunar illumination",             "lunar.illumination"),
  L = make_smooth_panel(cs, "yday",                "Day of year",                    "yday"),
  M = make_smooth_panel(cs, "avg_3day_prior",      "Previous 3-night avg count",     "avg_3day_prior")
)
 
# --- 1d. Roost type — categorical, point-range panel ---
roost_levels <- unique(fit$data$roost_type)
template <- fit$data[1, , drop = FALSE]

num_cols <- names(fit$data)[sapply(fit$data, is.numeric)]
for (col in num_cols) {
  template[[col]] <- median(fit$data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

new_roost <- template %>%
  select(-roost_type) %>%
  crossing(roost_type = roost_levels) %>%
  mutate(local_date = seq_len(n()))

preds <- fitted(
  fit,
  newdata = new_roost,
  re_formula = NA,
  incl_autocor = FALSE, 
  scale = "linear" # Link scale, so we can manually exp() it next
)

roost_ce <- new_roost %>%
  mutate(
    estimate__ = exp(preds[, "Estimate"]),
    lower__    = exp(preds[, "Q2.5"]),
    upper__    = exp(preds[, "Q97.5"])
  )
 
panel_roost <- ggplot(roost_ce, aes(x = roost_type, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__)) +
  labs(x = "Roost type", y = "Emergence size") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10)
 
# --- 1e. Spatial (colony location) — contour/heat panel like reference panel O.
# If you added gp(ctr_lon, ctr_lat), extract via conditional_smooths on that term;
# otherwise, approximate using colony-level mean fitted values plotted spatially.
 
colony_fitted <- track_df %>%
  mutate(fitted_val = exp(fitted(fit)[, "Estimate"])) %>%
  group_by(colony, ctr_lon, ctr_lat) %>%
  summarise(mean_fitted = mean(fitted_val), .groups = "drop")
 
# Determine the maximum value rounded up to a clean cutoff
max_val <- ceiling(max(colony_fitted$mean_fitted, na.rm = TRUE) / 100000) * 100000
break_vals <- seq(100000, max_val, by = 100000)

panel_spatial <- ggplot(colony_fitted, aes(x = ctr_lon, y = ctr_lat)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = mean_fitted, size = mean_fitted)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    limits = c(min(colony_fitted$mean_fitted, na.rm = TRUE), max_val),
    breaks = break_vals,
    name = "Predicted mean daily emergence size",
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1) # Forces color to merge with the size legend
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    limits = c(min(colony_fitted$mean_fitted, na.rm = TRUE), max_val),
    breaks = break_vals,
    name = "Predicted mean daily emergence size" # Must match the color name exactly
  ) +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
# NOTE: this is a discrete colony-level scatter, not a smoothed spatial surface.
# If you added a gp() term, a smoother contour can be built by predicting fit
# over a fine lon/lat grid instead — ask if you'd like that version.
 
## --- Assemble full panel grid, matching reference figure layout ---
final_panel <- wrap_plots(
  c(panel_list, list(N_roost = panel_roost, O_spatial = panel_spatial)),
  ncol = 4,
  byrow = FALSE) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
 
ggsave("./Figures/full_fs_ar_model_panel.pdf", final_panel,
       width = 16, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

# BAM

```{r}
# 1. Order data properly for AR structure: within colony-year time series
track_df <- track_df[order(track_df$colony, track_df$year, track_df$yday), ]

# 2. Mark the start of each colony-year series (bam's rho resets here)
track_df$series_id <- interaction(track_df$colony, track_df$year, drop = TRUE)
track_df$AR.start <- !duplicated(track_df$series_id)

# 3. Fit an initial model WITHOUT rho to estimate the AR1 coefficient from residuals
m0 <- bam(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ 
    roost_type +
    s(avg_3day_prior) + s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum.2m.night) +
    s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination) +
    s(avg_drought_index) +
    s(yday, bs = "cc") +
    s(yday, colony, bs = "fs", xt = list(bs = "cc"), k = 8) +  # colony-specific phenology
    s(dist) +
    s(colony, bs = "re") +
    s(year, bs = "re"),
  data = track_df,
  method = "fREML",
  select = TRUE,
  discrete = TRUE,
  nthreads = 4
)

# 4. Estimate rho from lag-1 autocorrelation of residuals, within series only
r0 <- residuals(m0)
rho_est <- acf(r0, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]   # crude global estimate; see note below
rho_est

library(dplyr)
rho_by_series <- track_df %>%
  mutate(resid = r0) %>%
  group_by(series_id) %>%
  filter(n() > 5) %>%
  summarise(rho1 = acf(resid, plot = FALSE, lag.max = 1)$acf[2]) %>%
  pull(rho1)

rho_est <- mean(rho_by_series, na.rm = TRUE)
rho_est
```

```{r}
m_ar <- bam(
  log(track_90q_count) ~ 
    roost_type +
    s(avg_3day_prior) + s(air.2m.night) + s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night) + s(prate.night) + s(rhum.2m.night) +
    s(pres.sfc.night) + s(tcdc.night) + s(lunar.illumination) +
    s(avg_drought_index) +
    s(yday, bs = "cc") +
    s(yday, colony, bs = "fs", xt = list(bs = "cc"), k = 8) +
    s(dist) +
    s(colony, bs = "re") +
    s(year, bs = "re"),
  data = track_df,
  method = "fREML",
  select = TRUE,
  discrete = TRUE,
  rho = rho_est,
  AR.start = track_df$AR.start,
  nthreads = 4
)

summary(m_ar)

# itsadug is built for exactly this diagnostic on bam AR models
library(itsadug)
acf_resid(m_ar)   # should show near-zero autocorrelation at lag 1+ now
```

```{r}
colony_resid <- aggregate(residuals(m_ar) ~ colony, data = track_df, FUN = mean)
coords <- unique(track_df[, c("colony","ctr_lon","ctr_lat")])
colony_resid <- merge(colony_resid, coords, by = "colony")

library(ape)
dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist(colony_resid[, c("ctr_lon","ctr_lat")]))
inv_dist <- 1 / dist_mat
diag(inv_dist) <- 0
Moran.I(colony_resid$`residuals(m_ar)`, inv_dist)
```

# Xgboost

exploratory pipeline using xgboost for predictive benchmarking plus iml's H-statistic for interaction detection

```{r}
library(xgboost)
library(iml)
library(recipes)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# 1. Prep data — grouped train/test split to respect structure
# ============================================================
# Split by series_id (not random rows) so temporal blocks stay intact,
# matching the CV approach used for the brms comparison — this keeps
# the RF/xgboost benchmark honest and comparable to the brms kfold results.

set.seed(123)
series_ids <- unique(track_df$series_id)
test_series <- sample(series_ids, size = round(0.2 * length(series_ids)))

train_df <- track_df |> filter(!series_id %in% test_series)
test_df  <- track_df |> filter(series_id %in% test_series)

# Predictor set — same environmental drivers as the brms model,
# excluding IDs/dates/response and anything that would leak (e.g., track_count_se)
predictor_vars <- c(
  "roost_type", "avg_3day_prior", "air.2m.night", "air.2m.night.diff",
  "wind_speed.night", "prate.night", "rhum_resid", "pres.sfc.night",
  "tcdc.night", "lunar.illumination", "avg_drought_index", "yday", "dist", "from_sunset"
)

# xgboost needs numeric matrices — one-hot encode roost_type
rec <- recipe(~ ., data = train_df[, predictor_vars]) |>
  step_dummy(roost_type, one_hot = TRUE) |>
  prep()

train_x <- bake(rec, new_data = train_df[, predictor_vars]) |> as.matrix()
test_x  <- bake(rec, new_data = test_df[, predictor_vars]) |> as.matrix()

train_y <- log(train_df$track_90q_count)   # match response scale used in brms model
test_y  <- log(test_df$track_90q_count)

dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = train_x, label = train_y)
dtest  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = test_x, label = test_y)

# ============================================================
# 2. Tune via CV (lightweight grid — expand if compute allows)
# ============================================================
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  max_depth = c(3, 5, 7),
  eta = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1),
  subsample = 0.8,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8
)

cv_results <- purrr::pmap_dfr(param_grid, function(max_depth, eta, subsample, colsample_bytree) {
  params <- list(
    objective = "reg:squarederror",
    max_depth = max_depth,
    eta = eta,
    subsample = subsample,
    colsample_bytree = colsample_bytree
  )
  cv <- xgb.cv(
    params = params,
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = 1000,
    nfold = 5,
    early_stopping_rounds = 30,
    verbose = 0
  )
  tibble(
    max_depth = max_depth, eta = eta,
    best_iter = cv$best_iteration,
    best_rmse = min(cv$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)
  )
})

cv_results |> arrange(best_rmse)
best_params <- cv_results |> arrange(best_rmse) |> slice(1)
best_params

# ============================================================
# 3. Fit final model with best hyperparameters
# ============================================================
# Safely handle the best rounds variable (it's usually 'best_iteration' from xgb.cv)
nrounds_val <- if (!is.null(best_params$best_iter)) {
  best_params$best_iter
} else if (!is.null(best_params$best_iteration)) {
  best_params$best_iteration
} else {
  500 # fallback if neither exists
}

final_params <- list(
  objective = "reg:squarederror",
  max_depth = best_params$max_depth,
  eta = best_params$eta,
  subsample = 0.8,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8
)

xgb_fit <- xgb.train(
  params = final_params,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = nrounds_val,
  evals = list(train = dtrain, test = dtest),  # Updated from watchlist to evals
  print_every_n = 50
)

# ============================================================
# 4. Predictive performance — this is your RF/xgboost benchmark number
# ============================================================
pred_test <- predict(xgb_fit, dtest)

rmse <- sqrt(mean((pred_test - test_y)^2))
mae  <- mean(abs(pred_test - test_y))
r2   <- cor(pred_test, test_y)^2

cat("Held-out (series-grouped) performance:\n")
cat("RMSE:", round(rmse, 4), "\n")
cat("MAE: ", round(mae, 4), "\n")
cat("R2:  ", round(r2, 4), "\n")

# This R2/RMSE, on the SAME held-out series_id folds, is what you compare
# against brms kfold() results — apples-to-apples on temporally honest splits.

# ============================================================
# 5. Variable importance
# ============================================================
importance_matrix <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_fit)
print(importance_matrix)
xgb.plot.importance(importance_matrix, top_n = 15)
```

Interaction detection with iml

iml needs a Predictor wrapper and works on a data frame (not the xgboost matrix directly), so reconstruct a clean data frame with matching columns:

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 6. Set up iml Predictor object
# ============================================================
# iml needs a data.frame of predictors + a prediction function.
# Use a manageable subsample for interaction analysis — H-statistic
# computation is O(n) per pair and gets slow fast on 20k+ rows.

set.seed(123)
iml_sample <- train_df[sample(nrow(train_df), min(2000, nrow(train_df))), predictor_vars]

# Predict function must replicate the exact preprocessing (dummy encoding) used in training
predict_fn <- function(model, newdata) {
  newdata_baked <- bake(rec, new_data = newdata) |> as.matrix()
  predict(model, newdata_baked)
}

predictor <- Predictor$new(
  model = xgb_fit,
  data = iml_sample,
  y = log(train_df$track_90q_count[sample(nrow(train_df), min(2000, nrow(train_df)))]),
  predict.function = predict_fn
)

# ============================================================
# 7. Overall interaction strength per variable (H-statistic, 1-way)
# ============================================================
# This tells you WHICH variables are most involved in interactions overall,
# before testing specific pairs — a good triage step since testing every
# pairwise combination (13 choose 2 = 78 pairs) is expensive.

interact_overall <- Interaction$new(predictor)
plot(interact_overall)

interact_overall_df <- interact_overall$results |> arrange(desc(.interaction))
print(interact_overall_df)

# ============================================================
# 8. Pairwise H-statistic for top-flagged variables
# ============================================================
# Take the top 4-5 variables from step 7 and test all pairs among them,
# rather than all 78 possible pairs — keeps this tractable.

top_vars <- interact_overall_df$.feature[1:5]
top_vars

pairwise_results <- list()
for (v in top_vars) {
  interact_2way <- Interaction$new(predictor, feature = v)
  pairwise_results[[v]] <- interact_2way$results |> arrange(desc(.interaction))
}

# Combine into one summary table
pairwise_summary <- bind_rows(pairwise_results, .id = "anchor_var") |>
  arrange(desc(.interaction))

print(pairwise_summary)

# ============================================================
# 9. Visualize the strongest flagged pair(s) with 2D partial dependence
# ============================================================
# Pick top 2-3 pairs from pairwise_summary and inspect their PDP surface
# to see the SHAPE of the interaction (this informs how to specify t2()/ti()
# in the brms model — e.g., is it a simple threshold interaction, or genuinely
# smooth/curved non-additive structure?)

top_pair <- c(pairwise_summary$anchor_var[1], pairwise_summary$.feature[1])
top_pair

pdp_2way <- FeatureEffect$new(
  predictor, 
  feature = c("pres.sfc.night", "roost_type"), 
  method = "pdp"
)
pdp_2way$plot()


pdp_2way_2 <- FeatureEffect$new(predictor, feature = c("pres.sfc.night","air.2m.night"), method = "pdp")
pdp_2way_2$plot()

# ============================================================
# 10. Single-variable PDPs for the top individual predictors
# ============================================================
# Compare shapes against your brms smooth term shapes — similar nonlinear
# patterns here vs. in conditional_smooths(fit) is a good cross-validation
# that both modeling approaches are picking up the same underlying signal.

for (v in importance_matrix$Feature[1:6]) {
  pdp_1way <- FeatureEffect$new(predictor, feature = v, method = "pdp")
  print(plot(pdp_1way) + ggtitle(paste("PDP:", v)))
}

m_add <- bam(log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) +
    s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) +
    s(prate.night)+
    s(rhum_resid) +
    s(pres.sfc.night) +
    s(tcdc.night) +
    s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) +
    s(avg_drought_index) +
    roost_type +
    s(dist) +
    s(from_sunset) +
    s(yday), 
    data = track_df, method = "fREML")
m_int <- bam(log(track_90q_count) ~ s(air.2m.night) +
    s(air.2m.night.diff) +
    s(wind_speed.night, k = 12) +
    s(prate.night)+
    s(rhum_resid) +
    s(pres.sfc.night) +
    s(tcdc.night) +
    s(lunar.illumination, k = 15) +
    s(avg_drought_index) +
    roost_type +
    s(dist) +
    s(from_sunset) +
    s(avg_3day_prior) +
    s(yday)+
    s(pres.sfc.night, by = roost_type, k = 10), 
    data = track_df, method = "fREML")

AIC(m_add, m_int)

# so we should add the interaction term of pres.sfc.night x roost_type
```
